title: Judge the Judge: Building LLM Evaluators That Actually Work with GEPA — Mahmoud Mabrouk, Agenta AI
talk_summary: Mahmoud Mabrouk shows how to build LLM-as-judge evaluators calibrated against human annotations, using GEPA prompt optimization (genetic-style mutation/merge with Pareto-frontier selection) to evolve the judge prompt. He demonstrates on TauBench airline customer-support traces that a naive judge (61% accuracy, 98% compliant-biased) improves to ~74% after optimization, but stresses data quality, binary metrics, reasoning in annotations, and seed-prompt choice dominate results.

takeaways.technique: Binary per-defect judges instead of one holistic score
takeaways.what_they_do: Decompose evaluation into specific error-type judges (policy adherence, response style, info delivery, tool use) each returning true/false plus reasoning, rather than one 1-5 'success' judge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it does not make sense to have one LLM as a judge which is success... it will make it too complex and it's very hard to learn

takeaways.technique: Calibrate judges against human-labeled traces with GEPA
takeaways.what_they_do: Collect human annotations (verdict + reasoning) on real traces, then run GEPA's optimize-anything loop (seed prompt -> mutate/merge candidates -> evaluate on batches -> Pareto-frontier select) to evolve the judge prompt toward human agreement.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're going to build and optimize these LLM as judges that are calibrated with human annotations
takeaways.numbers: accuracy 69%->74% on validation; non-compliant recall/precision went from ~0 to nonzero; bias 98%->64%

takeaways.technique: Reasoning in annotations is required for learning
takeaways.what_they_do: Annotators must supply why a trace passed/failed, not just the label, because the optimizer uses that reasoning to infer the underlying policy.

takeaways.technique: Custom reflection template with domain prior
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of GEPA's default reflection prompt, write one that includes the judge verdict, ground-truth label, and instructions to extract real policy rules; also pick a seed prompt biased toward the majority class.

takeaways.technique: Big model for refinement, small model for judging
takeaways.what_they_do: Use an expensive model only for the offline prompt-optimization/reflection loop, and a cheaper model for the judge that runs at scale; small models failed as judges/refiners in his tests.
takeaways.numbers: experiments cost ~$200-300 in tokens; GPT-4o/mini/nano and DeepSeek tried; small models 'complete failure'

takeaways.technique: Overfit small first, instrument, then scale sampling
takeaways.what_they_do: Stop at the first optimization iteration, inspect generated candidates and reasoning traces, fix the reflection prompt, only then increase sampling/budget; also split train/validation by task to avoid leakage.
takeaways.numbers: ~200-300 iterations per experiment; 480 train / 112 validation traces
